manifesto_l2.current: The sun does not choose who it reaches.
manifesto_l2.A: The sun spends itself on every room equally.
manifesto_l2.B: The sun cannot aim — it can only rise.
manifesto_l2.C: Every window in the city faces the same sun.

inscription.current: You warm every room you enter — and rarely ask who warms you.
inscription.A: You warm every room you enter — and run on warmth nobody returns.
inscription.B: You lift rooms before deciding to — and cannot switch it off to rest.
inscription.C: You are the weather of every room — and weather is never thanked.

yourNature_desc.current: You walk into a room and people feel more at ease, more energized, more capable — without you trying to make that happen. The cost is that you give it constantly and almost never get asked if you're okay.
yourNature_desc.A: You walk in and the room lifts — easier, braver, more possible — without your trying. The light runs on you: given constantly, metered never, and no one thinks to ask what it burns.
yourNature_desc.B: The lifting isn't a decision — you enter, and the room's temperature changes before you've spoken. What can't be done is aiming it, or turning it off: the warmth broadcasts, even on empty.
yourNature_desc.C: Rooms turn toward you the way fields turn toward morning — nothing decided, everything warmed. And like the sun, you are looked at only in eclipse: the day itself goes unthanked.
